title: Ali Shar and Zumurrud

full_text:
Ali Shar was the generous son of an affluent merchant of Khorasan. Upon his father's death, false companions flattered him and squandered his fortune until he was left penniless. Abandoned by his summer friends, he wandered into the slave market, where an extraordinary maiden named Zumurrud was being auctioned.

Zumurrud was gifted not only with dazzling beauty, but with mastery of calligraphy, silk embroidery, and chess. Observing Ali Shar’s honest countenance, she insisted that he purchase her, giving him her own hidden purse of a thousand dinars to pay the price.

Through her exquisite embroidery, which Ali Shar sold at high profit, their fortunes were restored, and they lived in mutual affection and peace.

However, a treacherous neighbor who envied their happiness abducted Zumurrud while Ali Shar was away in the market. Escaping her captors by cutting her hair, dressing in the armor of a prince, and mounting a swift Arabian stallion, Zumurrud rode across the desert to an unknown kingdom.

Arriving at the capital just as the elderly king had died without an heir, the citizens, following an ancient oracle, proclaimed that the first horseman to pass through the city gates should be crowned monarch. Zumurrud, disguised as Prince Emerald, was crowned with the royal diadem!

She governed the kingdom with peerless justice, establishing grain storehouses, building hospitals, and protecting the poor. Remembering her beloved Ali Shar, she instituted a weekly public banquet where every traveler in the city was invited to dine in the royal presence.

Months later, Ali Shar, who had wandered across deserts searching for his bride, entered the hall in rags. Recognizing him beneath his dust, Queen Zumurrud descended from the throne, revealed her identity, and made Ali Shar king beside her, celebrating a reunion forged in unwavering fidelity.
moral: Steadfast fidelity, courage under trial, and resourceful intelligence reunite separated lovers.
